'''Surface Mining''' is a Live-mode planetary activity introduced with the [[Rhino]] in Elite Dangerous update 4.4.1.0. Commanders locate a '''Planetary Mining Location''', deploy the Rhino from a compatible carrier ship, extract deposits with reusable mining rigs, refine the output aboard the vehicle, and transfer the resulting cargo to the ship.<ref name="frontier-4410">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/updates/4-4-1-0 Elite Dangerous – 4.4.1.0 Update Notes], Frontier Developments, 3 September 2026. Accessed 11 September 2026.</ref>

The ordered controls, rig placement, collection, recovery, and cargo-transfer sequence belongs to [[Surface Mining with the Rhino]].

== Activity mechanics ==

=== Planetary Mining Locations ===

Planetary Mining Locations are surface points of interest detected by mapping a landable planet or moon with a [[Detailed Surface Scanner]]. They do not appear on every landable body.<ref name="frontier-4410" />

Frontier describes these locations using several independent balance values:<ref name="frontier-4410" />

* site size;
* deposit density;
* deposit capacity;
* weighted commodity availability;
* deposit regeneration;
* a temperature effect on mining output; and
* the frequency of additional Microresource drops.

These values make two locations on the same body potentially different mining prospects. Frontier has not published exact generation ranges or output formulae.

=== Deposits and mining rigs ===

Inside a Planetary Mining Location, the Rhino's [[Planetary Mineral Scanner]] reveals mineable deposits on the terrain and sensors. Its Mining Rig Deployment Module places automated rigs over valid deposits, and several rigs can operate simultaneously.<ref name="frontier-release">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/rhino-available-now-arx-early-access Rhino – Available Now Via ARX Early Access], Frontier Developments, 2 September 2026. Accessed 11 September 2026.</ref>

A deposit has limited capacity and replenishes slowly after extraction.<ref name="frontier-dev-log">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/elite-dangerous-august-dev-log-2026 Elite Dangerous: August Dev Log 2026], Frontier Developments, 27 August 2026. Accessed 11 September 2026.</ref> Update 4.4.1.1 increased the maximum output of a mining rig from 9 chunks to 12.<ref name="frontier-4411">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/updates/4-4-1-1 Elite Dangerous – 4.4.1.1 Update Notes], Frontier Developments, 3 September 2026. Accessed 11 September 2026.</ref>

The Rhino refines collected chunks into commodity cargo through its built-in refinery. Frontier lists 72 tonnes of cargo capacity for the released vehicle.<ref name="frontier-store">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/store/vehicles/rhino Rhino], Elite Dangerous Gamestore, Frontier Developments. Accessed 11 September 2026.</ref>

=== Location economy ===

Surface-mining locations are finite working sites rather than permanent unlimited sources. Deposit capacity limits immediate extraction, regeneration governs how quickly deposits return, and the local commodity weighting determines which resources are more likely.<ref name="frontier-4410" />

A commodity being available at a location does not guarantee the same yield from every deposit. Valuable output must also be transferred from the Rhino to a carrier ship before it can be transported or sold.

== Requirements ==

A complete surface-mining operation requires:

* a ship supported by the [[Large Planetary Vehicle Hangar]];
* a fitted Large Planetary Vehicle Hangar carrying a Rhino;
* a Detailed Surface Scanner for locating Planetary Mining Locations;
* free cargo space aboard the carrier ship; and
* enough time to collect rig output and recover deployed rigs before leaving the site.

The released hangar supports classes 2–6 on most compatible ships and classes 2–4 on the Keelback. The exact ship list belongs to [[Large Planetary Vehicle Hangar#Compatibility|Large Planetary Vehicle Hangar § Compatibility]].<ref name="frontier-release" />

== Relationship to other surface activities ==

Surface Mining is distinct from:

* collecting loose raw materials with an [[SRV]];
* breaking ordinary surface outcrops;
* asteroid mining in planetary rings; and
* scavenging Odyssey settlements or crash sites.

Those activities use different locations, equipment, and reward loops. The Rhino may travel across ordinary planetary terrain, but its mining rigs operate on deposits inside Planetary Mining Locations.
